question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $C,$ defined by $x∼y$ if ${x}^{4}={y}^{4}.$ Which of the following equivalence classes contain the element $i?$

I. $[-1]$

II. $[-i]$

III. $[2i]$
question.worked_solution:
We have $i\in [x]$ if $i∼x.$ Using the definition of the given equivalence relation, we require

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{4} & ={x}^{4} \\ 1 & ={x}^{4} \\ {x}^{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $i\in [-1]$ because $(-1)^{4}=1\,✓$

- $i\in [-i]$ because $(-i)^{4}=1\,✓$

- $i\notin [2i]$ because $(2i)^{4}=16\ne 1\,\times $

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
